notes: US name 'Razr Ultra (2025)' and global name 'Razr 60 Ultra' are ONE physical device. Proof from the manufacturer on both sides: motorola.com/us .../razr-ultra/pmipmhn40ms and motorola.com/gb .../razr-60-ultra/pmipmhn42m1 publish the same closed dimensions (73.99 x 88.12 x 15.69) and the same 199 g, and Motorola's own launch release is titled with the paired name 'razr 60 ultra/razr ultra' and repeats that pairing six times. OPEN DEPTH LEFT NULL - TWO PRIMARY PAGES DISAGREE: motorola.com/us states 'Open: 73.99 x 171.48 x 7.29mm' while motorola.com/gb states 'Open: 73.99 x 171.48 x 7.19mm' for the same device. Height and width agree, so only depth is null; both sources are listed above rather than picking one. (For reference, Motorola gives 7.19 mm for the 2026 Ultra, but that is a different model and was not carried over.) Dimensions on 2025 pages are printed unlabelled and width-first; mapped as width 73.99 / long-axis height. Main display diagonal is Motorola's '7.0"'; note Motorola's 2026 Ultra page gives 6.96" for its own panel - no number was carried between generations. Resolutions recorded [width, height] ('2992 x 1224' is printed height-first); the cover pair '1272 x 1080' is kept in Motorola's order as no orientation is stated. materials.frame quote is a footnote on the GB page. announced/released via a web.archive.org snapshot dated 2025-12-13 of Motorola's April 24, 2025 press release; motorolanews.com returns HTTP 403 to direct fetching. May 15 is the US on-sale date. hinge.crease null - Motorola never names the crease shape. || EVIDENCE SWEEP 2026-09-13: these values were present in the research pass but carried NO sources[] entry covering their field, so they were set to null per the registry rule (a value without a citation is an assertion, not evidence). Preserved verbatim here so a human can re-source rather than re-research: hinge.type = 'flip'; hinge.axis = 'short'.
